testCases.description: Repository layer: Basic update operations for single and multiple fields

scenarios: Update single field (full_name) returns updated user object
Update multiple fields (full_name, phone_number, location_name) in single query
Update with empty object {} performs no operation and returns original user
Update non-existent user ID (e.g., 999999) returns null
Update skill_level from 'beginner' to 'intermediate' succeeds
Update location fields (location_lat, location_lng, location_name) together
Update profile_image_url with valid URL
Query excludes password_hash from returned user object
edgeCases: Update with same values (no actual change) still triggers updated_at
Update with NULL for optional fields (e.g., phone_number = NULL)

testCases.description: Repository layer: Database constraints and transaction integrity

scenarios: Update username to duplicate value throws UNIQUE constraint error
Update status to invalid value (e.g., 'deleted') throws ENUM constraint error
Update skill_level to invalid value (e.g., 'pro') throws ENUM constraint error
Update with transaction rollback on constraint violation (rollback test)
Update preserves other fields when partial update fails
Update inactive user (status='inactive') returns null (only active users)
edgeCases: Concurrent updates to same user row (optimistic locking test)
Update during database connection interruption

testCases.description: Repository layer: Automatic updated_at timestamp trigger validation

scenarios: Update any field triggers updated_at to change to current timestamp
updated_at is different from created_at after update
Multiple consecutive updates show increasing updated_at timestamps
updated_at precision is timestamp with timezone
created_at remains unchanged after update operation
No-op update (same values) still updates updated_at timestamp
edgeCases: updated_at within 1 second of NOW() after update
Timezone consistency for updated_at

testCases.description: Controller layer: Authorization checks ensuring users can only update own profile

scenarios: User with id=123 can update own profile (req.user.id=123, params.id=123) returns 200
User with id=123 cannot update other profile (req.user.id=123, params.id=456) returns 403
req.user missing (no JWT) is handled by middleware, but controller checks anyway
req.user.id type coercion (string '123' vs number 123) handled correctly
Non-existent user ID (params.id=999999) returns 404 before authorization check
Inactive user (status='inactive') returns 404, not 403
Suspended user (status='suspended') attempting update returns 404
edgeCases: req.user.id is null or undefined (malformed JWT payload)
params.id is non-numeric string (e.g., 'abc') returns 400

testCases.description: Controller layer: Field stripping and business logic validation

scenarios: Request body includes 'id' field - stripped before database update
Request body includes 'created_at' field - stripped before update
Request body includes 'password_hash' field - stripped before update
Request body includes 'email' field - stripped (email updates require separate flow)
Only updatable fields (full_name, phone_number, skill_level, location_*, profile_image_url, preferred_radius_km) are processed
Empty request body {} results in 200 with no changes (no-op update)
Request body with only non-updatable fields results in no-op update
Valid partial update with mixed updatable + non-updatable fields strips non-updatable
edgeCases: Request body with nested objects (e.g., {user: {full_name: 'X'}}) - reject or flatten
Request body with array values in scalar fields

testCases.description: Validation layer: Zod partial schema for PATCH operations

scenarios: Schema allows empty object {} (all fields optional)
Schema allows single field update (e.g., {full_name: 'John Doe'})
Schema validates phone_number format (e.g., '+1234567890' valid, 'abc' invalid)
Schema validates profile_image_url as valid URL format
Schema validates skill_level enum values ('beginner', 'intermediate', 'advanced', 'expert')
Schema validates status enum values ('active', 'inactive', 'suspended')
Schema validates location_lat as decimal between -90 and 90
Schema validates location_lng as decimal between -180 and 180
Schema validates preferred_radius_km as positive integer
Schema rejects unknown fields not in schema definition
edgeCases: Schema handles undefined vs null for optional fields
Schema trims whitespace from string fields
Schema validates maximum string lengths (full_name max 100 chars)

testCases.description: Route integration: Successful update flows with complete middleware chain

scenarios: PATCH /api/users/123 with valid JWT (user_id=123) and {full_name: 'New Name'} returns 200 with updated user
PATCH /api/users/123 with multiple fields {full_name, phone_number, location_city} returns 200
PATCH /api/users/123 with empty body {} returns 200 with unchanged user (no-op)
Response includes updated_at timestamp that is more recent than request time
Response excludes password_hash field
Response includes all user fields including email (own profile)
PATCH updates are immediately visible in subsequent GET /api/users/:id request
edgeCases: PATCH with Content-Type application/json header required
PATCH with very large request body (near size limit)

testCases.description: Route integration: Error responses and validation failures

scenarios: PATCH without Authorization header returns 401 Unauthorized
PATCH with malformed JWT token returns 401 Unauthorized
PATCH with expired JWT token returns 401 Unauthorized
PATCH to other user's profile (id mismatch) returns 403 Forbidden
PATCH to non-existent user ID returns 404 Not Found
PATCH with invalid payload (e.g., skill_level='invalid') returns 400 Bad Request with details
PATCH with malformed JSON returns 400 Bad Request
PATCH with non-numeric user ID (e.g., /api/users/abc) returns 400 Bad Request
edgeCases: PATCH with missing Content-Type header
PATCH with charset encoding issues (UTF-8)

testCases.description: Database integration: Transaction handling and rollback scenarios

scenarios: Update operation uses database transaction (BEGIN/COMMIT pattern)
Constraint violation triggers ROLLBACK (e.g., duplicate username)
Partial update failure rolls back all changes (atomicity test)
Successful update commits transaction and persists to database
Database trigger (updated_at) fires within same transaction
edgeCases: Transaction deadlock detection and retry
Transaction timeout handling (long-running update)
Nested transaction behavior (if supported)

testCases.description: End-to-end field stripping: Non-updatable fields are ignored at all layers

scenarios: PATCH with {id: 999, full_name: 'New'} - id is stripped, full_name updates, id remains unchanged
PATCH with {created_at: '2020-01-01', full_name: 'New'} - created_at stripped, remains original
PATCH with {password_hash: 'hack', full_name: 'New'} - password_hash stripped, remains original
PATCH with {email: 'new@test.com', full_name: 'New'} - email stripped (requires separate flow)
PATCH with only non-updatable fields {id, created_at, email} returns 200 with no changes
GET after PATCH confirms non-updatable fields remain unchanged
edgeCases: PATCH with all possible non-updatable fields in single request
PATCH attempts to set id to NULL or 0

testCases.description: Security: IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) attack prevention

scenarios: User A (id=1) with valid JWT attempts PATCH /api/users/2 returns 403 Forbidden
User B (id=2) with valid JWT attempts PATCH /api/users/1 returns 403 Forbidden
Attacker with valid JWT for id=1 cannot modify id=2 by sending {id: 2} in body (stripped + 403)
JWT token for user_id=1 attempting PATCH /api/users/1 succeeds (own profile)
Authorization check occurs BEFORE any database write operation (fail-fast)
edgeCases: JWT claims user_id as string '1' vs numeric 1 (type coercion test)
JWT with admin role (future) - currently should still fail for other users

testCases.description: Security: SQL injection and XSS prevention in update fields

scenarios: PATCH with SQL injection in full_name (e.g., "'; DROP TABLE users;--") is escaped/parameterized
PATCH with XSS payload in full_name (e.g., "<script>alert('xss')</script>") is stored safely
PATCH with SQL injection in location_name is parameterized
Parameterized queries prevent injection in WHERE clause (user id check)
Database returns injected strings as literal text, not executed
GET after PATCH returns XSS payload as plain text, not executed
edgeCases: Unicode characters in update fields (emoji, non-ASCII)
Null bytes in string fields

testCases.description: End-to-end: Complete user profile update flow with verification

scenarios: User registers → Login → PATCH profile → GET profile → Verify changes persisted
User login → PATCH full_name → Logout → Login again → GET profile → Verify persistence
User PATCH location fields (lat, lng, name) → Verify in database → GET profile confirms
User PATCH skill_level from 'beginner' to 'intermediate' → Verify in response and database
User attempts PATCH other user → Receives 403 → Original user profile unchanged
edgeCases: PATCH during concurrent GET request (read consistency)
Multiple PATCH requests in rapid succession (last write wins)

testCases.description: Regression: GET endpoint still works correctly after PATCH implementation

scenarios: GET /api/users/:id returns updated data after PATCH operation
GET field-level access control (own vs other profile) still works after PATCH changes
GET response excludes password_hash after PATCH (security regression check)
GET with sports data still returns correct sports array after profile PATCH
edgeCases: GET immediately after PATCH (no delay) returns fresh data

testCases.description: Performance: PATCH endpoint response time and database efficiency

scenarios: PATCH single field completes in under 100ms (p95)
PATCH multiple fields completes in under 150ms (p95)
100 sequential PATCH requests complete in under 10 seconds
edgeCases: PATCH with database connection pool exhaustion
PATCH performance with database indexes active
